---
title: "Story 3: Gun law strength and firearm mortality"
author: "Muhammad Suffyan Khan"
output: html_document
---

The full explanation is in the Jupyter notebook. The standalone chart script needs only base R; knitting additionally needs knitr and rmarkdown.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
```

```{r create-charts}
source("scripts/create_heatmaps.R")
```

The state maps now include direct takeaways, printed law levels, and numbered outlines linking Hawaii, Mississippi and New Mexico to their annotations. The mortality-band heat map prints state counts and within-group percentages, with color encoding the percentage on a fixed 0-to-100 scale. Black outlines emphasize the F group at 16 or more deaths (15/22, 68%) and the A group below 8 (7/13, 54%). This makes the message visible on the chart and accounts for unequal group sizes. Rounded cell percentages may not sum to 100%.

```{r show-charts, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("figures/01_law_strength_heatmap.png", "figures/02_firearm_mortality_heatmap.png", "figures/03_law_by_mortality_count_heatmap.png"))
```
